m.d: An ocean is a large area of salt water.
m.e: My great grandfather came across the Atlantic ocean from Scotland to Canada in 1882 on a sailing ship.

m.d: An occasion is a particular time.
m.e: Often she had to rush home on occasions when she might have preferred to stay out.

m.d: An occasion is a good time to do something.
m.e: The visit to Ottawa was a good occasion for us to get together.

m.d: An occasion is a special time or event.
m.e: Nov 12 is a happy occasion. It is my 25th wedding anniversary.

m.d: If x occasions y, x causes y.
m.e: Now we come to the problems that have occasioned this meeting.

m.d: October is the tenth month of the year.
m.e: There are 31 days in October.

m.d: If something occurs, it happens.
m.e: Over the summer a change occurred in my friend’s behaviour.

m.d: If something occurs to you, you suddenly think of it.
m.e: It occurred to me that I was in trouble.

m.d: If something happens occasionally, then it happens sometimes, but not often.
m.e: I occasionally get nosebleeds when I fly.

m.d: An occupation is a job or a career.
m.e: Nursing has been described as a skilled occupation rather than a profession.

m.d: An occupation is when a people, especially an army, take over and stay in a country, area, building, etc.
m.e: Everything he owned was taken during the German occupation of Paris in 1940.

m.d: An occupation is a hobby or something else that you do to pass the time.
m.e: Her favorite occupation is reading.

m.d: An octopus is an animal (a mollusc) that has eight arms.
m.e: I saw an octopus in the sea.

m.d: Occasional things happen every now and then, but not often.
m.e: Other than occasional attempts to draw him out, she respected his privacy.

m.d: If something occupies a space, it is there, lives there, or belongs there.
m.e: Her personal apartment has two bedrooms. In New York this is sometimes more space than entire families occupy.

m.d: If a country or army occupies another country, it controls it.
m.e: We have requested the removal of armed forces from territories occupied in the recent war.

m.d: If you occupy a position, you do a job, or have a job title.
m.e: Women are seeking positions that were formerly occupied by men.

m.d: The occult is anything to do with things that are not normal; supernatural or paranormal.
If you occult something, you cover it.
m.e: The Earth occults the Moon when a lunar eclipse happens.

m.d: If something is occult it is hidden or secret—or it is about hidden or secret things.
m.e: I've seen many occult happenings, including ghosts and witchcraft.

m.d: An occurrence is one case of something happening.
m.e: Meeting her became a daily occurrence.

m.d: About or by your job
m.e: Their income is: state pension £83.25 occupational pension £45.20 Total £128.45.

m.d: An octave is the interval between one musical pitch and another with double (or half) its frequency.
An occupant is a person who lives or works in a place, such as a house or office.
m.e: Joe Biden is the current occupant of the Oval Office.
